question.text: Kaveri Real Estate AIF has engaged its Sponsor-affiliate brokerage as the fund's custodian. A DD team flags this. Under Ch 12's 'Engagements with Third-party Service Providers' framework, the investor's concern is BEST described as:

answer.text: SEBI prohibits any service provider engagement between AIF and Sponsor affiliates.
Potential conflict of interest through related-party transactions — interests of the service provider may not be aligned with fund investors, and terms of contract need scrutiny.
Custodians cannot be engaged for Cat II real-estate AIFs at all.
The arrangement is automatically a breach of fiduciary duty.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 requires investors to 'verify potential conflicts of interest with all service providers, in form of related party transactions, understand the important terms of contract and verify that the interests are aligned'. Related-party is not prohibited but requires rigorous disclosure and pricing justification. The Trap: A, C are fabricated bans. D overstates — related party is a disclosure-and-arm's-length issue, not automatic breach. Cross-Exam Context: Related-party transaction framework also in III-A/C (Compliance) and XXI-B (PM — custodian appointment). XIX-C nuance: the PPM must disclose and the Investor Committee (or LP advisory board) may need to consent. Manager's Pro-Tip: When using Sponsor affiliates, benchmark fees against 3 external quotes, document in IC minutes, and disclose in PPM. LP Advisory Board sign-off provides an additional defence against later LP complaints.
